reasoning: Standard Palestinian thanks to a host after a meal, addressed to a woman with the -i endings. غيرو has long ee and a final o.
Loanword used in every Ramallah cafe; the MSA قائمة الطعام is not said. Stress on the first syllable, final u short-ish but written as the و in the spelling.
Active participle with long aa then short i. Used in Palestinian conversation for a fancy hotel or restaurant.
Shadda doubles the ج; taa marbuta after د is e. Often specifically a prayer rug, but used for rugs generally.
ق is a glottal stop, and the taa marbuta of حديقة is a after it. عامة has a doubled م and ends in e.
Two short a vowels. In Palestinian the commonest everyday sense is a wedding celebration, with 'joy' the abstract sense.
In Levantine speech the article assimilates to ج, which is now a sibilant: ij-jaww. حلو is 7ilu with a final short u.
The final taa marbuta is not heard in isolation: 7ama. It reappears with a suffix, 7amaati 'my mother-in-law', which is how the word is usually said.
Inherited numeral root, so ث is t in urban Palestinian and is respelled ت (compare تلاتة talaate). The final cluster takes an epenthetic i.
ما negates the existential fii, and 7ada is the Palestinian 'anyone'. Long ii in fii.
The verbal noun loses its first short vowel in Palestinian: rkuub, with long uu.
A religious term, so ق keeps [q] in this sense. Spelled the same as 'ible 'a kiss', which does glottalise; the English settles which word is meant.
Long aa in the last syllable. Urban Ramallah speakers who have no interdental say ghasayaan or ghatayaan, so the ث is the uncertain part here.
بلدية رام الله is everyday vocabulary. The -iyya suffix is -iyye, with shadda on the ي.
ق is a glottal stop at the end of fustu'. Literally 'Aleppo nut', the normal Palestinian name for pistachio; plain fustu' is peanut.
ض is emphatic D. Regular a-a past tense.
Word-initial hamza is not romanized. btiiji is the b-imperfect of إجا with long ii.

vowelled_arabic: إِلّي بِطْلَع مِن الدَّار بِقِلّ مِقْدَارُو
reasoning: b- plus yiTla3 contracts to biTla3; د is a sun letter, so id-daar. Both ق in بيقل and مقدارو are glottal stops.
Long ii then long aa, with the -iyye ending. Ordinary word for a household or office budget.
Long ee in the first syllable, written kasra plus ya. The unit noun means both a single olive and an olive tree.
Initial cluster bd-, long aa. Commonly extended as bdaal-ma before a verb.
Shadda doubles the ب, long uu, and taa marbuta after ل is e.
ق glottalises in this everyday word (مقابلة شغل). Taa marbuta after ل is e.
Form II of فضي, 'he emptied it out', used of letting a matter drop. Both ض are emphatic D; I am less sure of this idiom than of the pronunciation, as خلص الموضوع is commoner in Ramallah.
In this learned borrowing ذ is realised z in urban Palestinian (ustaaz), so it is respelled ز. Used as an address term for a female teacher, which is what the English 'miss' is after.
